chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hakam Al-A'ma and Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar Al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding a man who said to another man, 'O son of the fornicator' (meaning adultery), he (peace be upon him) said: 'If his mother was alive and present, then she came to claim her right, he would be whipped eighty lashes; and if she was absent, he would be awaited until she arrived so she could claim her right; and if she had died and nothing was known of her except goodness, the fabricator would be whipped the prescribed punishment of eighty lashes.'

key_terms.الْفَاعِلَةِ: The fornicator (female), used in the phrase 'son of the fornicator'
key_terms.شَاهِدَةً: Present and witnessing (as opposed to absent)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for calling someone 'son of the fornicator' and how does the mother's status affect it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific application of the hadd punishment for qadhf (slander) when the accusation targets a man's lineage by calling him 'ibn al-faqiha' (son of the fornicator). It highlights the mother's central role as the claimant of her honor, with the punishment of eighty lashes contingent upon her presence, absence, or verified posthumous righteousness, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the preservation of lineage and maternal dignity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Hakam Al A’ama and Hisham Bin Salim, from Ammar Al Sabaty, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding a man who said to a man, ‘O son of the (sexually) active’, meaning the adultery. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If his mother was alive, present, then she comes seeking her right, he would be whipped eighty lashes; and if she was absent, she would be awaited with until she proceeds, so she seeks her right; and if she had died and nothing was known from her except for the goodness, the fabricator would be whipped, upon him being eighty lashes’.
